$comment: Ratcheted quality budgets (issue 578). Enforced by `npm run verify:budgets`.
1. CI fails when a measured value EXCEEDS its budget. Existing debt never blocks
work; only adding to it does.
2. CI also fails on UNCLAIMED SLACK - a value measurably better than its budget
without the budget being lowered. Without this the ratchet stops ratcheting and
the gate silently degrades into a no-op.
3. Every change to a value REQUIRES `finding` and `justifiedBy` to be updated.
A budget moved without a cited finding and commit is not reviewable.
Every initial value was transcribed from a committed artifact under audit/, never
typed from memory. The first transcription attempt read contaminated artifacts left
behind by the mutation harness and produced 74/16/88/1703; the harness now restores
clean artifacts and asserts no mutant marker survives. These are the clean figures.

themeMatrixUntraceableRate.justifiedBy: issue 625, two defects fixed together, both in this gate's own machinery rather than in the rendered page. (1) The oracle: this sweep tracks color/background-color/border-color/border-radius/padding/font-size/font-weight/box-shadow/transition-duration/outline-width, but only ever probed a token's resolved value through FOUR CSS properties: color, padding-top, border-top-width, font-size. A token whose only expression is a font-weight, a box-shadow or a transition-duration shares no value space with any of those four, so it could never appear in the oracle - every element rendering it, even correctly from a real token, was misclassified untraceable. Brought to parity with the shared render classifier's probe set (render-capture.mjs), which already covered these categories. (2) Mantine's ScrollArea ships its own static scrollbar padding/transition in ScrollArea.css ('padding: calc(--scrollarea-scrollbar-size / 5)', a 150ms transition), untouched by any GDS theme override; both classifiers now exempt it by selector (mantine-ScrollArea-scrollbar/-thumb) rather than inventing a token for browser-chrome geometry that was never a design decision. Measured rate fell 26.83 -> 15.67 (26368 properties, 4133 untraceable) on the same 52-cell sweep, same commit, same tree - not a design fix, two broken rulers replaced. Two more fixed in the same investigation, both real: Chrome serializes a resolved color-mix() as color(srgb r g b / a), never rgb() - the same fix already shipped once for the identical reason in verify-badge-contrast-runtime.mjs. And Mantine's own border-top-width: calc(0.0625rem * var(--mantine-scale)) formula is now resolved and indexed directly, rather than left permanently untraceable because it combines a literal with a variable instead of referencing one custom property (both classifiers recognize the same resolvable Mantine constant; a border-top-style must be set on the probe first, or the UA reports 0 regardless of the declared width - the same lesson as the outline-width fix, applied to a second property). Final: 15.4% (26368 properties, 4061 untraceable), same 52-cell sweep.
themeMatrixUntraceableRate.$comment: The old headroom is gone. This sat at 34 to clear an observed 33.94-33.96 band with element counts varying by ~114 between runs, which meant a genuine 0.05pp regression was indistinguishable from noise. The band was render timing, not measurement error. The artifact now records exact counts rather than bucketing them to the nearest thousand, because reproducibility is what makes that precision honest. KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than implied: 36 of the cells hit the 400-element sample cap, so those routes are sampled rather than swept exhaustively - the true rate could differ on the unsampled remainder. cellsTruncatedAtSampleCap in the artifact reports it every run.

untraceableRenderRate.justifiedBy: issue 627: this rate had drifted from its 7.2% baseline without the classifier changing - a fresh Phase 1 re-run on the SAME 40 cells measured 9.857% (28962/293814), observation count up ~53% and literal count up ~110% since the baseline, meaning new content since the last correction is disproportionately untokenized. Investigated rather than silently ratcheted: closed four real, verified gaps in this pass. (1) render-capture.mjs itself had the theme-matrix oracle's exact gap class - TRACKED checked font-size and all four border-radius corners and both gap axes with no matching probe; fixed. (2) The color-mix()/color(srgb...) serialization gap (see themeMatrixUntraceableRate). (3) A naive value.split(',') shredded any multi-value transition-timing-function containing 2+ comma-separated cubic-bezier() functions mid-parenthesis ('cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), cubic-bezier(...)' became eight unmatchable fragments) - the single largest fix this pass; replaced with a paren-depth-aware split. (4) Mantine's border-top-width hairline formula, recognized directly (see themeMatrixUntraceableRate). Two real, GDS-owned literals also fixed at the source, not the classifier: .gds-tour-launch/.gds-tour-btn/.gds-tour-card__actions (packages/gds-theme/styles.css) now reference --gds-space-*/--gds-font-size-* tokens instead of bare rem values, and PublicShell's headerVariant='compact' now references --gds-space-3xl (the only one of its three header heights that lands exactly on an existing step). Result: 9.857% -> 7.428%, closing 91% of the regression. Follow-up: PublicShell's other two header heights (72px, 88px) were never a rounding candidate - no existing space step lands close enough without a visible resize - so a small, fixed (not per-theme) --gds-shell-height-* token set was added instead (resolveGdsShellHeightTokens, gds-theme/axes.ts), formalizing the shipped 64/72/88 values exactly as-is rather than redesigning them. Wiring it into the token-graph validator's category inference (token-operations.ts's inferNodeCategory, which classifies by role prefix) was required - an unclassified prefix defaults to 'color' and then fails the color-pattern check against a plain '72px' value, which is what the graph validation test caught. Result: 7.428% -> 7.418%. The remainder is understood, not unexplained: several Mantine components (SegmentedControl, Button-inner) declare component-scoped custom properties or plain literal transitions this methodology cannot see from a document-body probe, the same limitation already diagnosed for Badge's font-size; .gds-tour-card__progress's letter-spacing has no GDS tracking/letter-spacing token axis to reference at all; and a few individually small remaining literals (Stack-root's Mantine-derived gap, a sidebar width literal) were not chased further. Render mutants M1/M2 remain the validity proof of the instrument.

touchTargetFloorViolations.justifiedBy: issue 628: a live sweep of all 26 routes measuring every interactive element against GDS's own documented 44px floor (GDS_MIN_TARGET_PX, axes.ts) found real, non-zero debt - CardContracts.ts computes a resolved minTouchTarget per card and nothing read it. Fixed at the source in the same pass: three genuinely unsized ActionIcons (DocsCodeBlock's copy button, NumberStepper's +/- controls, ProductCard's overflow menu), gds-admin's PageHeader overflow menu (was size='lg'=34px), ListingCard's save/share affordances (were size='lg'=34px - the exact card this whole investigation started from), and ThemeToggle's default size (was Mantine's unreviewed 'md'=28px, now 'xl'=44px, a header control rendered on every route). KanbanBoard's and GdsRichTextEditor's dense-toolbar controls got a data-gds-target-exception marker rather than resizing - their rows are packed tightly enough (GdsRichTextEditor's toolbar gap is 4px) that padding out the hit area risked adjacent controls overlapping, which GDS_CONTROL_HEIGHT_EXCEPTIONS' own 'where the control stands alone' caveat already anticipates. AdvancedDataTable's isolated checkbox and VibeThemePicker's 32px theme-swatch grid (the single highest-leverage fix, one component behind 50 of the original 146 mid-severity findings) both got a real 44px hit area via an invisible-padding CSS technique that doesn't grow the visible control. The dominant remaining contributor, by a wide margin, is the site's own NavLink component: 247x41px and 221x25px instances alone account for roughly 250 of the 791 remaining violations, appearing on every route via the primary/sidebar navigation. That is a real, single-root-cause, systemic finding, not noise - but fixing it means visibly growing the whole navigation's row height, which is a deliberate design decision this pass did not make unilaterally. Recorded as the clear next target, not silently accepted as unfixable. Issue 629 closed that target, and its premise was half wrong: 247x41 was NavLink, but 221x25 is Mantine `Text` rendered as a link - a different component with a different fix, carried separately. NavLink needed no design decision at all: GDS's own density axis already declares `controlHeights.md` as 44px and `resolveGdsDensityTokens` clamps it to GDS_MIN_TARGET_PX under every density mode, so the row height was already specified and NavLink simply had no theme entry consuming it. `gdsTheme.components.NavLink.styles.root.minHeight` now reads `var(--gds-control-height-md)` (packages/gds-theme/src/theme.ts), which propagates to every lane through `extendGdsTheme`'s `mergeThemeOverrides` - asserted per lane in theme.test.ts rather than assumed. Measured 791 -> 564 across the same 26-route sweep, with NavLink-root findings at exactly zero afterwards. The visible change is 41px -> 44px per navigation row. Issue 659 closed the next target: the recorded parent/display classification showed all 286 sampled a.mantine-Text-root findings were genuine discrete targets, none exempt under WCAG 2.5.8, and traced both dominant shapes - the card title link and its "Open section" footer link - to one shared component, ReferenceLinkGrid.tsx, used across seven playground surfaces. Fixed with the same invisible-padding technique issue 628 established for the checkbox and swatch grid (.gds-touch-target-pad-link, inset -12px, data-gds-target-exception), safe here in a way the swatch grid was not automatically safe: each anchor sits inside a Paper p="lg" in a SimpleGrid spacing="lg", so the padded hit area has no neighbor within 12px in any direction - no overlap to accept. Measured 564 -> 268 across the same 26-route sweep (296 findings cleared, more than the 286-finding sample estimated, from routes/locales the sample did not cover).
touchTargetFloorViolations.$comment: This budget is intentionally NOT wired as a hard-fail chain member (unlike badge-contrast/forced-colors-runtime): the gate measures and writes the artifact (verify:touch-target-floor-runtime, informational, always exits 0), and this budget entry is what actually enforces the ratchet, matching the themeMatrixUntraceableRate/untraceableRenderRate pattern exactly. A same-day zero-tolerance gate would have hard-failed the build over debt requiring its own deliberate remediation, not a rushed one.

tokensWithGaps.justifiedBy:
issue 710: 87 -> 86, back down. --gds-bg-page's demoed gap and --gds-motion-ease-standard's explained gap both closed as a side effect of QuickStartCard's real consumption and documentation of them (CHANGELOG.md/COMPONENTS_AND_PATTERNS.md) -- neither token's count changed since both still carry a remaining gap, but --gds-motion-duration-base regressed from 0 gaps to 1 (useCase): adding a new, earlier CHANGELOG mention of it (the QuickStartCard hover transition) pushed forward-trace's first-occurrence-only useCase window off the prose that used to satisfy it elsewhere in the doc corpus. Fixed at that new first occurrence instead of just re-justifying the number: CHANGELOG.md's QuickStartCard paragraph now states directive usage prose ('use this pair for the shared base-speed/standard-ease transition rather than a component-local duration') inline where the token is actually introduced. Net: 87 -> 86, tightened down to the newly-measured value per this budget's own established discipline (see the issue 618 entry below).

issue 698: 78 -> 87. The new layout axis emits 9 --gds-layout-* tokens; all 9 land as gaps. This is the same structural ceiling every non-color axis already hits, not a regression unique to this change: measured directly against the current tree, sibling motion/density tokens carry the identical gap shape (e.g. --gds-motion-duration-instant fails demoed/explained/useCase; --gds-density fails demoed/variationsShown/useCase) because forward-trace.mjs's publishedRoles set is built from each DTCG group's top-level keys only (packages/gds-theme/src/generate-dtcg-tokens.mjs nests every non-color axis, layout included, one level down under .semantic), so variationsShown can only ever reach its fallback branch (a literal token-name match in playground source) for a token in this class -- 87 of 92 tokens in the whole system are gapped today, a ~95% rate this issue's 9 tokens simply join. Of the 9, listed and explained already pass (CHANGELOG.md/COMPONENTS_AND_PATTERNS.md/THEME_GOVERNANCE.md document all nine in prose). demoed passes for the 4 tokens DiscoveryShell/BottomTabBar actually consume today (sidebar-width, header-height, footer-height, bottom-bar-height); the remaining 5 (nav-item-height, content-max-width, list-rail-width, content-bottom-padding, sheet-top-radius) have no real consumer yet by design -- issue 698 itself states its own axes.layout declaration on a real preset, and any component adoption beyond DiscoveryShell/BottomTabBar, are out of scope and land in already-filed issues 702 (SidebarNav) and 707 (browse canvas); sheet-top-radius has no bottom-sheet component in gds-core yet to consume it. Forcing a consumer into DiscoveryShell/BottomTabBar for content-max-width or content-bottom-padding just to satisfy this heuristic was rejected: neither is requested by issue 698's scope, and adding an unrequested maxWidth/paddingBottom constraint to every existing DiscoveryShell consumer's main content area would be a real, unreviewed visual regression, not a documentation fix. This ratchet retires back toward 78 as 702/707 land and give those 5 tokens a real consumer.
tokensWithGaps.$comment: Issue 612 RESOLVED for the drift half: forward-trace.mjs and dimensions.mjs now run inside artifacts:refresh, so this artifact is regenerated every cycle instead of only when someone remembered to run audit:refresh. The caveat this comment used to carry - that the true gap was this figure OR MORE - no longer applies. Proof the drift was real: the committed dimensions.json recorded 1293 site phrase keys while the packs held 1297. 612 CLOSED: the 9 gaps (focus-ring x4, density, identity-unresolved, motion-duration-ambient, transition-scope, text-on-support) are classified in scripts/audit/forward-trace.config.mjs with verified reasons and review dates (2026-11-01). Classified means explained, not excused - they still count here, and this ratchet only moves down by actually closing one.

unreachableTokens.justifiedBy: issue 586: all 15 F13 tokens classified — 14 extension points with reasons and expiry dates, 1 pending wire-up tracked as issue 591. 0 remain unclassified.
unreachableTokens.$comment: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE ZERO. 0 does NOT mean 'no unreachable tokens exist' — 15 tokens are still referenced by nothing. It means 0 are UNCLASSIFIED. The gate's job is that no token can be declared without a written, dated disposition; it is not that every token renders. The classification counts (extensionPoints, pendingWireUp) are in the same artifact and are the numbers to read for remediation progress. Measurement also changed source here: the old value came from forward-trace.json#/rows[!demoed] (Phase 2 demo reachability, a different question) and is now the reachability census. Stated per the F24 rule.

publishedGraphOverlap.justifiedBy: issue 595: badge tone pairs add 20 roles. Issue 593: the accent axis adds 50 roles. Issue 558: the reaction axis adds 14 roles. Issue 557: the typography and elevation axes add 34 roles. Issue 556: the density axis adds 16 --gds-space-*/--gds-control-height-*/--gds-density roles. Issue 555: the shape axis adds 21 --gds-radius-* roles (7 steps + 14 semantic roles) to the 34 from issue 585. All 55 runtime semantic roles are published per theme per scheme; coverage 55/55 = 100%.
publishedGraphOverlap.$comment: Was 1 — the published graph and the runtime semantic set overlapped only on `accent`, so a design tool importing the graph received 17 atmosphere colours and none of the roles that determine what a component looks like. Direction is `min`, so this can only go up: dropping a semantic role from the published graph now fails the release.

undeclaredMantineDependencies.justifiedBy: issue 589 census: 92 consumed, 4 governed by gdsTheme, 6 delegated with reasons, 1 dynamic, 8 lane-only, 73 ungoverned. Budget = 73 ungoverned + 8 lane-only. Ratcheted 81 -> 80 (issue 597): LabelTag stopped rendering a raw Mantine palette colour as text, removing one ungoverned consumption. Claimed rather than banked — the slack left the mantine-governance mutant alive, since adding a variable back landed inside the unclaimed headroom and the gate stayed green.
undeclaredMantineDependencies.$comment: MEASUREMENT CHANGED in issue 589, stated rather than slipped in (the F24 lesson). The old value 87 came from dimensions.json#/themeControl/mantineVarsGdsConsumesButNeverDeclares and meant 'consumed but never DECLARED as a CSS custom property'. The new value means 'consumed but not DICTATED by the default gdsTheme', measured by comparing gdsTheme against Mantine's DEFAULT_THEME, with reasoned delegations excluded. 87 -> 81 is NOT 6 variables remediated: nothing was declared and no rendered value changed. The two counts answer different questions, and only the new one distinguishes a value GDS actually controls from one it merely writes down.

registryAtomsWithoutCoverage.justifiedBy: issue 581 - every registry kind is now either obligation-modelled or explicitly covered elsewhere with a named gate/phase. NOTE: the MEASUREMENT CHANGED. It previously counted atoms in kinds with no audit-phase coverage (1699); it now counts atoms in kinds with neither an obligation model nor a recorded owner (0). The 1699 did not vanish - 410 of those atoms have real unmet obligations and are tracked by the separate obligationGaps budget below.

localesWithoutSitePack.justifiedBy: issue 587: ja, ko and zh site phrase packs generated through the existing generator, so every package locale now has a site pack. Parity is enforced BETWEEN the corpora by verify:locale-coverage — the gap existed because coverage was only ever verified within each corpus separately.

englishLeakageWorstLocale.justifiedBy: issue 611: the seven Hebrew phrases the endpoint could not translate now carry owner-approved translations, so he dropped to 0 and the worst site locale is de at 0.15% (three English loanword phrases German renders verbatim, budgeted in i18n-leakage.config.mjs).
englishLeakageWorstLocale.$comment: MEASUREMENT CHANGED, stated per the F24 rule. The old 3.8% counted every value byte-identical to its English source. That put ~46 non-defects per pack into the number: emails, `Cmd+1`, `npm run verify:references`, component-name lists, and in the package corpus genuine cognates - `Pause`, `Filter` and `Message` are real German and French words. Of 15 package values it flagged, ONE was a real defect. The metric now requires peer evidence that the phrase is translatable (another locale rendered it differently, compared on letters only so an Arabic comma is not mistaken for a translation) plus a script-aware test: any English left in a non-Latin pack is a miss, while a Latin pack is only flagged for prose. The two numbers answer different questions and must never be compared. Remaining: 7 in site/he that machine translation cannot resolve (issue 611) and 2 German loanword phrases, both recorded with reasons in scripts/i18n-leakage.config.mjs.

phase5MutationScore.justifiedBy: Issue 601: renamed from `gateMutationScore`, which read like the GATE SUITE's score and pointed at the Phase 5 render mutants. One word, three referents — the trap F24 named. audit Phase 5 - 6/7 killed, M3 survives, 5 not run, commit bed78c8

renderMutationScore.justifiedBy: issue 579 - M1 and M2 both killed; Phase 1 is only trustworthy while these stay killed

gateSuiteMutationScore.justifiedBy: The gate suite that verifies every OTHER gate was the one gate whose coverage could silently shrink: only `gateSuiteUnexplainedSurvivors` was ratcheted, and deleting a mutant does not raise it — a deleted mutant survives nothing, so the count stays 0 while coverage drops. Seeded at the measured 100% (29 of 29 killed) on 2026-08-13.

gateSuiteUnexplainedSurvivors.justifiedBy: issue 580 - every survivor must be either killed or filed with a dated issue

obligationGaps.justifiedBy:
issue 711: 356 -> 355, tightened down to the newly-measured value per this budget's own established discipline (a materially-better-than-budget measurement is supposed to lower the number, not sit on unused slack -- confirmed the hard way: leaving it at 356 let the obligation-coverage gate-mutation test's injected single-undocumented-prop mutant land exactly on the budget line (355+1=356<=356) and survive undetected, a real regression in gate coverage this fix restores). Net improvement traced to issue 711's own new exports (DetailFactsTable/ProviderCTA and SemanticButton's new label prop) all shipping with real JSDoc, plus incidental documentation of a pre-existing gap while touching neighboring code.

issue 656, first tranche: packages/gds-core/src/PartnerDiscovery.tsx was the largest single contributor at 51 of the 404 (72 files carried the rest). 48 of those are prop atoms and now carry member-level JSDoc; the remaining 3 are shareState variant atoms needing a playground demo, not a comment, and are untouched here. The docs state what the name cannot - which props are controlled and therefore must be supplied in pairs (email/onEmailChange, value/onQueryChange), that the map adapter renders but never filters, that backHref is a href rather than a callback so the back control is a real link, and that every onEvent is a privacy-safe hook with no built-in destination. Restating the prop name would have satisfied the gate and helped nobody, which Rule 17 forbids. A measurement note worth keeping: the first pass inserted each block with a trailing blank line, and the gate correctly refused to count 10 of them - its obligation is a JSDoc terminator on the line ABOVE the declaration, and a blank line between the two is not that. The gate caught its own tranche. Measured 404 -> 356 (prop 726/1054, variant 69/107, accent 10/10).

designRuleUnclassifiedRate.justifiedBy: issue 650: first real measurement from issue 649's audit/design-rule-coverage.json (25 presets x 2 schemes x 4 routes), transcribed not estimated. Worst preset: warm (73.6%). Advisory: a brand-new, single-release-old measurement mechanism, not yet graduated to blocking.
